lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Streaming a PC game to a Nintendo handheld that's more than a decade old. That's the experiment here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On a 3DS? Does that even work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's what moonlight-N3DS explores. It's Antoine's fork of a GameStream client for New 3DS homebrew, originally by zoeyjodon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The console receives the game stream from a PC, using the Moonlight approach. The code is a C plus plus client from the moonlight-embedded lineage.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It targets the New 3DS, not the original model, for the extra RAM and CPU headroom. And expect lower resolution and higher latency than streaming to a Switch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The page says the stars on this fork reflect Antoine's port experiments, which are still low. Community installs and discussion live upstream, where the original project has around three hundred stars.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's honest about where the action is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. To get started, the README on the n3ds-main branch and the moonlight-embedded wiki are the places to look.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's also a blog article on handheld streaming and homebrew, linked from the page.
